summary: Interpreted the executed snapshot-delta experiment (CheckRun 9cba2e79ff6c4019b0f0381690d9aaab, exit 0, tests_passed). Parsed index 0 is the discriminating control (store_last=4, snapshot_index=0, should_snapshot=false under the large threshold); parsed index 1 is the witness produced by the target's own snapshot path: the user Snapshot() succeeded and compaction emptied the log store (store_last=0) while the snapshot index advanced to 4, and should_snapshot became true even though commit_index and applied_index were still 4, so no new entry existed since the snapshot. Because runSnapshots calls takeSnapshot whenever the verdict holds and takeSnapshot only refuses when nothing at all was applied, the node re-creates a snapshot at an unchanged index each SnapshotInterval. Recorded as violated (defect_claim asserted) with the consequence explicitly bounded to redundant snapshot creation and IO at the unchanged index - no safety effect - plus limitations on the FSM-snapshot success prerequisite, the deterministic TrailingLogs=0 reachability, and the untested install-snapshot/monotonic-store variants.
